extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and peer reviewers of prediction model studies (regression or machine learning) in healthcare/biomedicine
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors and reviewers on transparent reporting of studies that develop, validate, or update multivariable prediction models for diagnosis or prognosis, applicable to regression and machine-learning approaches (including LLMs via TRIPOD-LLM).

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPOD+AI overarching purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: TRIPOD+AI is a 27-item checklist that aims to harmonise the landscape of prediction model studies and provide transparent reporting regardless of whether regression models or machine learning methods have been used. TRIPOD+AI supersedes the TRIPOD 2015 checklist, which should no longer be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to improve the transparency of reporting of a prediction model study regardless of study methods; use the 27-item TRIPOD+AI checklist rather than TRIPOD 2015.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Report essential information about the prediction model study in the title and abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure title/abstract clearly indicate the study involves development, validation, or updating of a prediction model (diagnostic or prognostic) and summarize target population, outcome, key predictors, and intended use as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background and Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide background and clear objectives, including target population, predictors, outcomes, and intended use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the clinical problem and rationale for the model, state whether the model is diagnostic or prognostic, and define the intended application and decision context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — Source of data
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the source(s) of data used to develop, validate, or update the model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report study design, data provenance, dates/period of data collection, and any linkage or aggregation procedures that affect generalisability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — Participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe participant eligibility, recruitment, and relevant baseline characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include inclusion/exclusion criteria, setting, care pathway, and flow of participants through the study (e.g., diagram), to allow assessment of representativeness and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — Outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the outcome(s) used for model development or validation, including timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise outcome definitions, measurement procedures, event timing, and any adjudication or censoring rules that affect outcome ascertainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — Predictors
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe predictor variables, how and when they were measured, and any pre-processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report full list of candidate predictors, measurement methods, any transformations, coding of categorical variables, and timing relative to outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — Sample size
rubrics_metrics.description: Report sample size considerations and justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide rationale for chosen sample size (including events-per-variable or other calculations), and discuss implications for model reliability and overfitting risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — Missing data
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how missing data were handled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report extent and patterns of missingness, methods used (e.g., complete-case, multiple imputation), assumptions made, and sensitivity analyses if performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — Analytical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe statistical or machine learning analysis methods used to develop, validate, or update the model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear details on model specification, predictor selection, tuning procedures, hyperparameter optimisation, internal validation (e.g., cross-validation, bootstrapping), and performance estimation methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — Class imbalance handling (new)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any methods used to handle class imbalance in outcome or label distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report sampling strategies, weighting, threshold selection, synthetic data generation (e.g., SMOTE), and justification for chosen approach and its impact on performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — Fairness considerations (new)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address fairness-related design and analysis choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report whether fairness was evaluated, which protected attributes were considered, metrics used to assess bias, mitigation strategies applied, and implications for deployment in diverse populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Science — Code availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Report availability of code used for data processing, model development, and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide link(s) to repositories, specify licence/conditions for reuse, and describe which parts of the workflow are reproducible from provided code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Science — Data availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Report availability of the data used in the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether data are publicly available, hosted in repositories, subject to access restrictions, or cannot be shared; provide information to request access where applicable and describe any synthetic/derivative datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Science — Pre-registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Report pre-registration or study protocols when available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide registration identifier or link to protocol, pre-specified analysis plans, and note any deviations from pre-registered methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient & Public Involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe involvement of patients or the public in study design, conduct, or dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report whether and how stakeholders contributed to defining outcomes, predictors, study aims, interpretation, or plans for communication and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results — Participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Report participant flow, sample characteristics, and numbers used in analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present counts for development/validation cohorts, missing data summaries, and baseline characteristics relevant to applicability and generalisability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results — Model development
rubrics_metrics.description: Report how the model was developed, including final model specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide details on predictor coefficients or model weights, model architecture for ML methods, hyperparameters, and any feature selection or pre-processing steps that define the final model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results — Model performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Report model performance using appropriate metrics and uncertainty estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include discrimination, calibration, decision-analytic measures where relevant, confidence intervals or other measures of uncertainty, and performance across subgroups if assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results — Model updating
rubrics_metrics.description: Report any model updating or recalibration performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe methods and results of updating (e.g., recalibration, model revision), rationale, and impact on performance and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion — Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss limitations of the study and model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address sources of bias, limitations in data, generalisability concerns, and consequences for interpretation and use of the model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion — Usability of the model in context
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss usability and applicability of the model in the intended clinical or operational context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider implementation needs, required inputs, integration into workflows, interpretability, and barriers to adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion — Implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe implications for clinical practice, policy, and future research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the model could be used, what evidence remains needed (e.g., external validation, impact studies), and potential harms or benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPOD-LLM extension — scope
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension addressing the unique challenges of LLMs in biomedical and healthcare applications; provides a comprehensive checklist of 19 main items and various subitems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use TRIPOD-LLM when the model is an LLM or LLM-based system; it emphasises additional reporting needs specific to large language models.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPOD-LLM — Explainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasise explainability for LLM-based systems in biomedical/healthcare contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report methods used to explain model behavior, limitations of explanations, and how explanations were validated or evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPOD-LLM — Transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasise transparency specific to LLMs (architecture, training data, fine-tuning).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report model provenance, training data characteristics, pretraining/fine-tuning procedures, and any public documentation to support reproducibility and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPOD-LLM — Human oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Report human oversight mechanisms for LLMs deployed in healthcare settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe expected human roles, review processes, escalation pathways, and safeguards to ensure appropriate use and to mitigate errors or harmful outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPOD-LLM — Task-specific performance reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Require task-specific performance reporting for LLMs applied to health tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide performance metrics relevant to the specific tasks (e.g., question-answering accuracy, factuality rates), uncertainty estimates, and subgroup analyses where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer use — Outcome definition and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should check that outcome definition and timing are clearly reported and appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether outcome ascertainment, timing, and any censoring are clearly described and appropriate for the intended clinical question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer use — Predictor measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should check completeness and clarity of predictor measurement reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure predictors are defined, measurement timing is reported, and pre-processing or coding steps are transparent and justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer use — Performance measures and uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should check that appropriate performance measures and measures of uncertainty are reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that discrimination, calibration, and where relevant decision-analytic measures are presented with confidence intervals or other uncertainty quantification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer use — External validation status
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should check whether external validation has been performed and its status clearly reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether external validation cohorts are described, how they differ from development data, and implications for generalisability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer use — Calibration assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should check that calibration assessment is reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for calibration plots, calibration-in-the-large, calibration slope, and discussion of miscalibration and any corrective steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer use — Decision curve / clinical utility analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should check whether decision-analytic or clinical utility analyses are provided when relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the presence and appropriateness of decision curve analysis, net benefit calculations, or other evaluations of clinical usefulness.
